newsitem.title: UK: UK small firms say red tape costs jobs.
newsitem.headline: UK small firms say red tape costs jobs.

text.p: Compliance with legal regulations is imposing an increasing burden on small businesses in Britain and costing jobs, according to a survey by the Forum of Private Business.

The survey, presented on the fringes of the Labour party annual conference, showed that the costs of "red tape" for a typical small company employing 15 people and with annual turnover of around one million stg were the equivalent of two percent of turnover.
"This equates to the cost of employing an extra person," the forum said.
It said the Conservative government's Red Tape Taskforce had failed to ease the burden on business and welcomed the Labour Party's pledge to make reducing red tape a priority issue.

The business forum called for different government agencies to be combined into a single inspectorate and for smaller companies to be allowed to calculate value-added tax on a turnover basis rather than on a transaction basis, as at present.
